repository_card.frontier: Reflection positivity, GNS reconstruction and Wilson certificates expose separate proof obligations; real poles alone are not certificates.
repository_card.bridge_hypothesis: Treat real-pole effective models as adversarial tests of the OS dictionary. Preserve the positive-time observable algebra and reflection form. Gauge-fixed fields, quantum channels and Euclidean Wilson observables have different positivity structures.
repository_card.next_finite_task: Build a small reflection Gram matrix for a toy transfer model and compare its PSD condition with propagator-pole reality. Separately check whether tree gauge fixing commutes with the chosen physical reflection.
repository_card.falsifier: A negative reflection quadratic form refutes the toy RP claim; failure of reflection compatibility blocks importing gauge-fixed positivity into WilsonRPCertificate.
repository_card.proposal_status: speculative; not executed or formally verified

sources.title: On Quasiparticles within the Refined Gribov-Zwanziger Model
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.source_claim: The refined Gribov-Zwanziger effective model is reexamined through PT symmetry, with a proposed interpretation of quadratic excitations in the real-mass-pole case.
sources.limits: An effective gauge-fixed propagator and real poles do not establish reflection positivity for gauge-invariant Wilson observables, OS reconstruction, or a physical mass gap.

sources.source_claim: Anshu and collaborators construct constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expanders with depth-one local circuit realizations and apply them to one-dimensional Hamiltonians with an entanglement-gap relation.
sources.limits: An expander gap, a transfer gap and a many-body Hamiltonian gap are different operators. Track dimension, locality and the definition of gap before translating. First posted 1 September.

sources.title: Efficient Quantum Simulations of Yang-Mills theory with Maximal-tree Gauge
sources.publication_status: preprint; peer-review status not established in this sweep
sources.review_depth: v1: abstract and maximal-tree gauge construction
sources.source_claim: Li and collaborators use maximal-tree gauge and field-amplitude digitization to obtain polynomial resource bounds for Hamiltonian Yang-Mills simulation through QSVT.
sources.limits: Hamiltonian simulation complexity is distinct from an exact Haar edge-coordinate equivalence, Euclidean reflection positivity, and a continuum mass gap. First posted 27 August; a September news mention is not a new submission.
